idea-plugin.name: AutoTyper - Live Coding Simulator
idea-plugin.description:
AutoTyper - Live Coding Simulator

Simulate realistic, structured typing of Java classes in the editor.

Perfect for live coding demonstrations in lectures and presentations. Instead of typing code line-by-line from top to bottom, AutoTyper types code in the natural development order — just like a real developer would write it.

✨ Key Features

  • Structured Typing with Step Markers — Define the typing order using simple // @step N comments in your Java files
  • Automatic File Creation — The plugin automatically creates the Java file in the correct package directory and opens it in the editor
  • Package-Aware — Detects package declarations and creates the proper directory structure
  • Keyboard Shortcut: Alt+N — Press Alt+N anywhere in IntelliJ to advance to the next step. Works even when the editor has focus!
  • Natural Development Flow — First the empty class, then fields, then constructor, then methods
  • Adjustable Speed — From slow (30 WPM) to turbo (600 WPM)
  • Auto-Pause Between Steps — Pauses after each step for explanations
  • Pause/Resume/Stop Controls — Full control during typing
  • Progress Indicator — Shows current step and overall progress

⌨️ Keyboard Shortcuts

Alt+NNext Step (works globally, even when editor has focus)

Customizable via Settings → Keymap → search "AutoTyper"

📝 How Step Markers Work

Add // @step N comments to your Java files:

// @step 1
package ch.demo;

// @step 1
public class Calculator {

// @step 2
    private double result;

// @step 3
    public Calculator() {
        this.result = 0;
    }

// @step 4
    public double add(double a, double b) {
        result = a + b;
        return result;
    }

// @step 1
}

🚀 Quick Start

  1. Place annotated .java files in ~/autotyper-snippets/
  2. Open the AutoTyper tool window (right sidebar)
  3. Select a file, adjust speed, click Start
  4. The file is auto-created and opened in the editor
  5. After each step: press Alt+N or click Next Step

💡 Tips for Lecturers

  • Use 100-150 WPM for a natural look
  • Enable auto-pause to explain each step
  • Press Alt+N to advance — works without switching focus!
  • Organize snippets in folders per lecture topic


Created by Rolf — info@rolfsblog.ch
